content.title: About
content.content: Fat back is the layer of fat located under the skin on the back of a pig. In cooking it is prized for its ability to melt into a rich, flavorful base for sautéing, braising, and adding moisture to dishes. When heated, the fat renders, creating a fragrant, silky texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Fat back is a staple in French, American Southern, and Eastern European cuisines.
It is the primary ingredient in traditional French lard (graisse de canard).
Chefs often use it to sauté vegetables for an extra depth of flavor.
It can be seasoned and stored as a flavored cooking fat.
In many regions it is used to make homemade sausages, pâtés, and confit.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Provides about 900 kcal per 100 g, making it a dense source of energy.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains thiamine (B1), riboflavin (B2) and cobalamin (B12), which support metabolism.

items.title: Fat‑soluble vitamin carrier
items.content: Helps the body absorb fat‑soluble vitamins A, D, E, and K from other foods.

items.title: Monounsaturated fats
items.content: Includes monounsaturated fatty acids that may support cardiovascular health when consumed in moderation.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Because it is very calorie‑dense, portion control is important, especially for weight management.

items.title: Saturated fat
items.content: A large proportion of the fat is saturated, and excessive intake can raise cholesterol levels.

items.title: Allergy or intolerance
items.content: Some individuals may react to pork fat, particularly if they have a pork allergy.

items.title: Product quality
items.content: Low‑quality fat may contain residues of antibiotics or hormones; choose reputable suppliers.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Render the fat back and use it for sautéing meats, vegetables, and potatoes, adding it to sauces, stews, and casseroles. It is also popular for making homemade pâtés, confit, and for frying bacon. Heat slowly to avoid burning.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep rendered fat back in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 weeks or in the freezer for up to 6 months. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.
